implementation_notes: ActiveRecord's association is the parent's mapper: has_many :lines, dependent: :destroy makes destroying the order destroy its lines, and accepts_nested_attributes_for :lines (with autosave implied) writes, updates and - with allow_destroy - deletes children atomically inside the parent's save transaction, so the child model needs no repository of its own. The child still carries a primary key because ActiveRecord requires one, but nothing should query it directly: that discipline is what makes it dependent mapping rather than a plain has_many. Use the plain association plus explicit child saves only when the child is a real entity.
code_sketch:
class Order < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :lines, class_name: "OrderLine",
           dependent: :destroy, autosave: true
  accepts_nested_attributes_for :lines, allow_destroy: true
end
# order.save / order.update write the lines in the same transaction;
# OrderLine is never queried on its own.
pitfalls: Without accepts_nested_attributes_for or autosave: true, saving the parent does not persist changed children - the association alone is only a query.
dependent: :destroy loads and destroys each child (callbacks, one DELETE per row); :delete_all is bulk but skips callbacks - pick deliberately.
Nested attributes without allow_destroy cannot remove a line, and a missing id creates a duplicate instead of updating: the _destroy contract is easy to get wrong.
